newsitem.title: USA: Judge rejects limits on questioning of DNC aide.
newsitem.headline: Judge rejects limits on questioning of DNC aide.

text.p: A federal judge on Monday denied a request by Democratic National Committee official John Huang to limit questioning by a conservative legal group in a civil lawsuit against the Commerce Department.

The ruling cleared the way for the group Judicial Watch to question Huang on Tuesday as a witness in its two-year lawsuit under the freedom-of-information law claiming the department failed to release requested documents on trade missions led by late Commerce Secretary Ron Brown.

The group claims the department used trade missions improperly to raise funds for Democrats. Huang, who has come under fire for campaign contributions he solicited as a DNC fundraiser, previously worked at the Commerce Department.

Federal judge Royce Lamberth rejected Huang's argument that the group wanted to question him for improper political reasons. "Mr. Huang has not shown any good cause for any particular limits on the questions that may be asked," he said.
In a four-page ruling, the judge refused to restrict questioning to the period from mid-1994 until late 1995 when Huang worked at the Commerce Department.

"The court does expect that the parties will act in a professional manner and will focus on the taking of an appropriate deposition regarding the adequacy of the search for documents" sought by Judicial Watch, Lamberth said.

At a court hearing earlier on Monday, Larry Klayman, the group's general counsel, denied charges by a DNC official that the latest developments were an effort by an extreme right-wing group acting for political purposes. "We are not looking to grandstand the deposition," he said.
But government lawyer Bruce Hegyi said during the hearing that Klayman in other depositions strayed far from the issues in the case.
John Keeney, a lawyer for Huang, told the judge his client was "ready and willing to go forward" with the deposition. Keeney on Sunday accepted the subpoena from Judicial Watch.
